_comment: Editable mana-equivalent heuristic. These are not claims about universal MTG card values; they are knobs for consistent goldfish decisions and strategy-relative comparisons.
_comment_color_category_multipliers_colo: v4.15.7 research finding (task #18): colorless cards are now floored at the WORST color already in the RELEVANT category's own table (min across that category's 5 values), not this flat constant - see ValueModel.color_category_multiplier's docstring for the Rosewater 'weakest color in that ability' citation. This value is kept only as a last-resort fallback for a category with no table entries at all (should not normally be reached).
_comment_resource_to_mana_conversion: v4.15.4: implements the fully-designed-but-0%-implemented resource-to-mana-conversion framework from Docs/DEFAULT_VALUES_AND_COLOR_PIE_v1.md Sec. 5.1/5.1.1 (mirrored in Data/Models/default_value_table_and_color_pie.json::resource_to_mana_conversion). Bucket A (life_as_cost_rate/delve_rate/convoke_improvise_rate): official WotC design rates (Phyrexian mana templating: 2 life = 1 mana; Delve/Convoke/Improvise keyword templating: 1 graveyard card/tapped permanent = 1 mana) - see ValueModel.life_as_mana_equivalent/delve_mana_equivalent/convoke_improvise_mana_equivalent. Sacrifice-as-cost has NO rate here on purpose - Emerge's own reminder text confirms it must be a dynamic lookup of the sacrificed card's own value (ValueModel.sacrifice_cost_equivalent), not a flat constant. stun_counter_mana_equivalent_rate is only the FALLBACK method (ValueModel.stun_counter_mana_equivalent_fallback); the PREFERRED method is stun_counter_value_discount_per_counter, a LOW-CONFIDENCE first-guess constant (ValueModel.stun_counter_value_multiplier) since no official WotC rate exists for stun counters, unlike life/delve/convoke. Suspend/Decayed/conditional-attack-restrictions reuse the general-purpose ValueModel.uptime_value_discount, no separate constants needed (design doc's own 'same bucket-B logic' conclusion). SCOPE BOUNDARY, same as boardwipe_scaling_discount above: value-estimation utilities only, NOT wired into the real cast/payment path (available_mana_value) - that would need the same not-yet-built alternative-cost-aware payment infrastructure as the boardwipe scaling estimator's own open note.
_comment_wincon_and_context: v4.14.0 (Route E): ValueModel.win_condition_preservation_multiplier (Docs/WINCON_AND_CONTEXT_VALUE_v1.md Sec. 2) applies a SOFT downward bias to how attractive it is to cast a card right now when it's a piece of a defined Win Condition, scaled inversely by how many WCs are defined and by a crude redundancy proxy (how many distinct cards that WC needs), floored at wc_preservation_floor_multiplier (0.5) so it can never become a hard lock. ValueModel.hand_board_context_multiplier (Sec. 3) boosts draw-role value on a near-empty hand and passive/engine-role value on a large board. HONESTY NOTE, stated in both docstrings and the concept doc's own Sec. 5: unlike the color-pie or vanilla-test calibrations, there is no external reference for any of these six constants - they are first, clearly-flagged starting estimates (same pattern as v4.9.3's x_spell_proximity_bonus_max), pending revisit once Data/Learned/engine_value_store.json has real accumulated history to check against. NOT wired into cast_score_v4/live sequencing in this version - reporting/utility functions only, same caution as Route D.
_comment_engine_value: v4.13.0 (Route D): ValueModel.engine_value blends a card's predefined, card-shape-only value (predefined_static_value) with a value LEARNED from real, persisted simulation history across ALL past runs (Data/Learned/engine_value_store.json, written by run_pipeline_v440 as engine_value.csv). Bayesian-shrinkage blend: engine_value_cold_start_pseudo_seen (30) is how many games' worth of trust the predefined estimate starts with - at learned_seen=0 (fresh checkout, or a card never yet logged) the result is byte-identical to the predefined value, same safety pattern as v4.11.0's color_identity=None fallback. engine_value_max_learned_weight (0.85) caps how far the learned side can ever dominate, even at huge sample size, because recorded metric events are themselves an incomplete picture of a card's real contribution (e.g. combat damage from a plain creature body isn't fully captured). Reporting-only in v1, NOT wired into cast_score_v4/live sequencing yet - see Docs/ENGINE_VALUE_v1.md for the full design and its explicitly stated scope boundaries.
_comment_keyword_weights: v4.12.0 (Route C): all keywords bundled under one additive 'Keywords' category per explicit user request (lump Lifelink etc. together rather than a separate knob per keyword-family) - keyword_value(card.keywords) sums every keyword's weight (not an average, so a card with 3 keywords is worth more than one with 1). Unrecognized/future keywords fall back to keyword_weight_default (0.25) rather than silently scoring 0. Weights are a first, reasoned estimate (evasion/protection keywords weighted above simple triggers) - not yet cross-validated against real card_impact.csv data the way the X-spell knobs were.
_comment_creature_body_value: v4.12.0 (Route C): power+toughness as a SUM (per the user's own suggestion, not tracked separately) times creature_pt_sum_rate. Calibrated via Mark Rosewater's 'vanilla test' - a fairly-costed vanilla creature has P+T ~= 2x mana value (e.g. a 3-mana 3/3), so at rate=0.5 a bare vanilla body's value ~= its own mana cost (net_value ~= 0 for 'just stats, no text'), leaving room for keywords/text to push a card above or below fair value. This replaces cast_score's old flat +1.0-for-any-creature heuristic, so creature size now actually differentiates sequencing.
_comment_instant_speed_premium: v4.12.0 (Route C, Baukastensystem): a flat additive bonus for instant-speed cards, reflecting the flexibility of holding up mana / responding on the opponent's turn vs. a sorcery-speed effect of otherwise equal value. Independent, separately-tunable knob (per the Baukastensystem principle) - not blended into any other metric.
_comment_boardwipe_scaling_discount: v4.12.0 (Route C): two-parameter effective-cost ESTIMATOR for self-scaling-cost board wipes (Blasphemous-Act-shaped: 'costs {1} less to cast for each creature you control', floored) - flagged as an open gap in the Red pilot. effective_cost = max(floor, base_cost - discount_per_creature * scaling_count). Confirmed via the project's own Scryfall cache that this card shape is real (March of Wretched Sorrow, Furygale Flocking both use 'less to cast for each' scaling). SCOPE BOUNDARY, stated plainly: this is a value-estimation utility only, used where the engine reasons about a card's worth - it is NOT wired into the live mana-payment path, same class of gap as Delve/Convoke/Improvise/Emerge (still unimplemented at the payment-mechanics level, see v4.11.0 notes).
_comment_color_category_multipliers: v4.11.0: scales draw/opponent_life_loss(burn)/removal/boardwipe/mana_generated(ramp) by how good the casting color is at that category, per the official WotC 'Mechanical Color Pie 2021' primary/secondary/tertiary classification (see Docs/DEFAULT_VALUES_AND_COLOR_PIE_v1.md and Docs/COLOR_VALUE_PILOT_v1_red.md for sources). 1.0 is a ceiling, not a boost: it means 'unchanged from the pre-v4.11.0 flat rate', so this can only hold a color/category combo at its old value or discount it for colors that aren't primary there - nothing scores higher than before. Multicolor cards use the best applicable color (max across color_identity); colorless cards are floored at the worst color already in the category's own table (v4.15.7, researched - see color_category_multipliers_colorless_fallback's own comment for the citation), not a flat guessed placeholder. opponent_life_loss's row is lower-confidence than the others: WotC's source discusses 'damage to creature/planeswalker/player' as one primary red ability without breaking out the player-damage share specifically, so this row is our own reasoned extrapolation from that same quote rather than a separately cited source.
_comment_color_category_multipliers_v4_1: v4.12.0 (Route B): every primary-color cell now has real EDHREC deck-inclusion data behind it, not just red - Wrath of God confirmed present in mono-white control (23%/312 of 1350 decks), Counterspell/Brainstorm/Psychosis Crawler etc. in mono-blue card-draw (3580 decks), Toxic Deluge/Damnation/Go for the Throat/Infernal Grasp in mono-black control (3560 decks), Llanowar Elves/Cultivate/Rampant Growth as the definitive mono-green ramp package (9000 decks, Rampant Growth itself at 38%/3410 decks - directly confirms the removal-category root reference card). One real adjustment came out of this: white's removal multiplier moved 0.70 -> 0.80 after the data showed Swords to Plowshares (75% incl., 1010 decks) and Path to Exile (68%, 912 decks) as white control's actual top cards - a cheap unconditional-EXILE removal shape (with a real cost: opponent gets a basic land or life) that the original 'destroy'-focused WotC quote undersold. Everything else in the table held up against real data without needing a change.
_comment_x_spell_value_mode: v4.9.2: best_x_plan's non-lethal ('value mode') search walks X from smallest to largest and takes the first X whose own net_value/ROI already clears x_min_net_value/x_min_roi - no separate overkill-discount knob needed (an earlier soft-cap decay here could crush a spell's value before it ever reached its own viable X; removed after real-run evidence showed it happening to White Sun's Zenith).
_comment_x_spell_proximity_bonus: v4.9.3: face damage stays deliberately cheap per point (opponent_life_loss_per_point=0.42, well under mana_unit) because chip damage that doesn't threaten to close out the game is weak value - that part is intentional, not a bug. x_spell_proximity_bonus_max adds a per-point bonus, scaled by how close this cast (times a potential Aziza/Mica copy) gets to the opponent's remaining life, so burn that's actually closing in on a kill is valued much higher than the same damage spread thin over a full life total. Starting calibration (1.0) is a first estimate, not yet cross-validated against a real run the way the other X-spell knobs were - revisit once real card_impact.csv data shows how Banefire/Crater's Claws actually get cast under it.
_comment_value_curve_exponents: v4.10.0: generalizes the diminishing-returns idea draw_curve already proves out for 'draw' to other metrics that were still flat/linear, via ValueModel.curved_count (effective = amount ** exponent; 1.0, the default for anything not listed here, reproduces the old flat-linear behavior exactly). Two directions, deliberately opposite: opponent_life_loss < 1.0 (diminishing) - a cheap efficient burn spell (Lightning Bolt: 3 damage/1 mana) is more mana-efficient per point than a huge X spell (Banefire), which a flat per-point rate couldn't express; this is separate from and additive with x_spell_proximity_bonus_max above, which is about closing in on an actual kill, not raw efficiency. creature_tokens > 1.0 (increasing) - a wide board of tokens is worth disproportionately more than the same tokens counted one at a time (board-wipe resistance, evasion/chump-blocking math, go-wide synergies). Both starting values are first estimates, not yet cross-validated against a real run - revisit once card_impact.csv data from a run with token/burn X-spells is available.
